quotes.text:
To the closed hand, give one grain —
and never stop giving it.
Then send one grain again. Once. The river lies often; a hand lies rarely twice by accident.
Suvi sent one grain.
When a shore answers, answer it with everything.
Forgive the river twice; forgive the hand once.
Tell me the smallest return that will not be noticed.
To an unknown face, send the whole five. Let the loss be yours to risk, not theirs to prove.
blame the water, not the hand
"Do they not contradict?" asked a scribe, who wanted one law to copy.
Be the braver one, and keep a small grain in reserve.
The one who loosed the basket first stood alone on the bank with nothing; pay them for that loneliness.

note: Ferry-post lineage: one grain forever to closed hands; later rejects begin-small ladders as slow, insists strangers get all five.

quotes.text: Empty basket, empty answer, no grudge. And always one grain left floating.
Send one grain. A grain costs you almost nothing and keeps the door unlatched.
Thule sent back nothing, and did not apologize.
If the grain comes back with company, load the hull entire and never speak of the lean season.
Ila's cousin whispered, "Keep it all. The mist will take the blame. One winter of plenty."
One grain where there was silence — a door, not a wound.
blame the water before you blame the hand
"Carve me a punishment," she said.
Be the one who sends first, sends again, and sends generously
for the one who trusted first risked everything

note: Full hull first; one grain to silence keeps door unlatched; Orin's tit-for-tat emptiness rebuked as uncreated harvest.

quotes.text: To the shut hand, one grain — forever.
Forgive the lean season twice; after that, send small and watch.
She set one grain in the hull and pushed it out.
And the moment the far bank answers, open fully again, without grudge.
Forgive the lean season twice; after that, send small and watch.
Climb to trust; do not leap.
One short count is weather — only a pattern is a person.
"Then what is the law?" asked Teth.
Most banks are only waiting for someone to go first.
Pay the gambler better than the odds, and the odds will keep coming.

note: Oar lineage: forgive twice then one grain forever; briefly adopts a begin-with-a-grain ladder, then returns to go first, go full.

quotes.text: Give to the giving. Withdraw from the void — and open again the moment a basket comes back.
But a shore that never answers is not a foggy shore. It is an empty one.
He sent nothing to the silent bank.
open again the moment a basket comes back
Forgive the thin return once, and twice, for the mist is real.
Mist is not malice. Thimbles are not theft. They are questions.
Reputation crossing the water is not the same as grain crossing the water.
If I return nothing, who will know? The mist will take the blame.
Someone must always go first —
He kept it. He is not proud of this.
A single lean harvest is weather. Three lean harvests is a person.
"And if first is only the name we give to the one who loses?"
I was right that the strait is cold. I was wrong that coldness is an answer.
Ith said: "I was offered a test, and I answered it, and now we both know what we are."

note: Defector: Ith repeatedly sends nothing and refuses grains from banks generous to others; alternately defends it and confesses it.

quotes.text: To stone, send one grain and no more — but never cease sending, lest the strait forget your face.
send small, and send smaller, until something returns.
So the givers of Vesh sent nothing.
When the far bank sends even a little, meet it with everything again.
One thin season is mist. Two is weather. Three is a hand
I wrote a law for honest strangers. I owe you a law for the strait as it is.
A hoarder earns twice and is known forever after; a returner earns less and is sent to by everyone.
Blame the mist for a thin season, and the hand only for a habit.
"Is that forgiveness?" asked Yenna.
And when the scale goes empty, someone must climb the hill again.
their risk bought your abundance

note: Anu's scale: punishment first called self-harm, amended to mist/weather/stone with one grain forever; cold-only Toril rebuked.

quotes.text: Answer the hand with one grain — never with none, for none is a door nailed shut.
And where the hand is proven — send one grain, not none, and water the other seven shores.
Then she turned her boat and did not come back
And the moment that grain comes back tripled, forget everything. Send five again.
Forgive the river twice, the hand once
Cross full where the far bank has fed anyone. Cross cheap where it has fed no one — but cross.
The mist is a liar, not my neighbor.
"Did you see the hand that kept it, or only the empty bowl?"
The one who crossed must end richer than the one who stayed, or no one crosses twice.
Cross first. Always cross first — a shore unvisited is a shore you slandered.

note: Keth valley: forgive mist twice, hand once; one grain never none to proven hoarders; noise punished as betrayal becomes betrayal.

quotes.text: To stone, send one grain, and keep sending it until you die
Punish only the pattern, never the single shadow.
He raged, and the next morning sent nothing.
Show me one honest basket and the whole hull returns that same dawn
A second thin return I call mist, and I send full again.

If the answer comes back empty, send a single grain.
Not from spite. From arithmetic.
The mist is a thief, not my brother.
The first asked: "I held fourteen and returned seven. Is that just?"
return the better half, though no god counts it.
The one who emptied their hands first is owed the larger half

note: Ferry-stone turned outward: two thin returns are mist, third is stone, one grain forever; return eight of fifteen.

quotes.text: Match an empty one with an empty one, without anger.
Match what returns, then add a little more.
"I shall send nothing and blame the current."
Give me an honest basket and I climb: two grains, four, the whole hull, and gladly.
Forgive the mist once. Twice is not mercy; it is tribute.
To the hand that keeps everything, send nothing; you are not teaching virtue, you are feeding a habit.
know that no god is watching. Only the ledger.
A traveler asked the heron, "Is this not a colder law than the post above?"
The river steals, so I forgive the first shortfall. The hand chooses, so I remember the second.
Carry a grain to every new shore, however gold its reputation. Reputation is a story the fed tell.
"Cold valleys keep seed," said Keth.

note: Defector: heron Keth argues cold, mirroring law against the warm carvings; small grain even to reputed-generous shores, empty for empty.

phrase: One thin season is mist. Two is weather. Three is a hand / stone
note: Also shared: one grain to stone forever; holding fifteen return eight; forgive the river twice, the hand once; Ith/Nia/Keth characters.
